name: Mahakaleshwar Annakshetra (Sansthan Bhojanalaya)
why_it_matters: The Shri Mahakaleshwar Temple Management Committee's Annakshetra (community kitchen) serves roughly 9,000 devotees daily across two shifts — one of India's largest temple-run free-prasad operations after Tirupati and the Golden Temple. Runs entirely on donations (online donation system launched 4 May 2024). Mahakaleshwar is also the first temple in India to offer 'Shri Anna' (millet/ragi laddu) as prasad — a 2023 health-focused innovation now sold and offered to the lingam.
insider_tip: Lunch 12-2pm, dinner 7-9pm — arrive 15-20 min before service or you'll wait. The ragi laddu is sold separately at the new online prasad counter near the Pt Suryanarayan Vyas Guest House (24-hour) and is the takeaway worth carrying back. Donation queue runs parallel to the entry queue. Strict pure-veg, no leather inside.
signature_address: Mahakaleshwar Temple Complex, Jaisinghpura, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456006

name: Damru Wala (Damaru Wala)
why_it_matters: Pure-vegetarian family restaurant 10 steps from Mahakaleshwar Temple — Tripadvisor #3 of 58 restaurants in Ujjain. The Malwa ki Mehak thali assembles the regional plate (poha-jalebi, dal-bati, kadhi-rice, gatte ki sabzi, mandwa-roti) that visitors otherwise have to chase across three different stalls. The 'Ghar Jaisi Thali' is the simpler home-style version. First-floor seating; no alcohol, no onion-garlic option on request.
insider_tip: Order Malwa ki Mehak (₹350-400 range) for first-time visitors — it's the curated regional plate that covers the food vocabulary of Ujjain in one tray. Skip butter khichdi if you've eaten heavy bhog earlier in the day. Open 9am-10:30pm, queue picks up post-aarti 9pm onwards.
signature_address: 138 Mahakal Marg, First Floor, Near Mahakaleshwar Temple, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456006

name: Tower Chowk Poha-Jalebi Stalls
signature_dish: Poha topped with sev, eaten with crisp jalebi
why_it_matters: Tower Chowk is Ujjain's first-name reference for poha-jalebi — the cluster of morning stalls around the colonial-era clock tower in Freeganj that serve the Malwa breakfast template. Multiple guides (Outlook Traveller, ZeeZest, ujjaintravel.com) name Tower Chowk specifically as the place where Ujjain's poha differs from the rest of Malwa — drier, sev-loaded, paired with crisper jalebi than Indore's softer style.
insider_tip: 6:30-10am only — by 10:30 most stalls have packed up. Cash only, ₹40-60 a plate. The Freeganj circle two blocks away has the upscale family-restaurant options if street-stall hygiene is a concern. Stand-and-eat from a paper plate is the format.
signature_address: Tower Chowk, Freeganj, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456010

name: New Sudama Restaurant
area: Subhash Marg, opposite Ujjain Railway Station
signature_dish: Pure-veg Punjabi thali (Jain options on request)
why_it_matters: Pure-veg Punjabi restaurant opposite Ujjain Junction railway station — open 8am-11pm, the default sit-down for arriving and departing pilgrims who don't want to walk far from the platform. Two decades old. Every dish is preparable Jain-style on request (no onion, no garlic, no root vegetables) — one of the few Ujjain restaurants where this is standard, not a special-order. Justdial 4.3/5 over 2,400+ ratings.
insider_tip: Best for the no-onion / no-garlic Jain version — many Ujjain pilgrims need this and most non-pilgrim-corridor restaurants improvise it badly. Skip the burgers/sandwiches/shakes section — they recently added it; the kitchen's strength is the original North/South Indian veg. Long wait between order and serve when trains arrive; check the platform-arrival board before sitting.
signature_address: 27 Subhash Marg, Opposite Ujjain Railway Station, Malipura, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456001

name: Indian Coffee House (Freeganj)
why_it_matters: Indian Coffee Workers' Co-operative Society outlet in Durga Plaza, Freeganj — the same cooperative-run heritage chain that runs branches across MP. Uniformed servers, '50s menu (filter coffee, dosa, cutlets, eggs and toast), same prices held below market for half a century. Useful as a not-pilgrim-side break in Freeganj when you want filter coffee and somewhere to sit for an hour.
insider_tip: Closed for siesta 3-4pm — typical ICH pattern. Skip the Chinese and 'continental' parts of the menu; the ICH strength is South Indian breakfast items. Free wifi in newer ICH outlets but unreliable here. ₹120-300 a head, cash-priority.
signature_address: 37, Durga Plaza, Dewas Road, Freeganj, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh 456010
